intendedObjective: Identify distracting clarity problems in the personal essay with minimal intervention.
acceptableEditScope: Only small clarity edits; preserve the exact calendar heading and the essay's modest account of progress.
stableFactsAndClaims: The narrator wants to cross the pool without checking proximity to the edge; the instructor shows where the shallow lane ends.
Adults attend for different reasons; nobody demands explanations of childhood or fear.
The narrator paid for six lessons, struggles to relax while floating, and can put their face in and exhale steadily by the third lesson.
Crossing still involves stops for breathing or reassurance that stopping is possible; the instructor distinguishes these reasons.
Lessons occur in a municipal pool; another course or practice with a friend remains undecided.
The narrator can briefly look at blue tiles in mid-lane without needing the edge.
ambiguity: The narrator has not chosen what to do after the last lesson.
voiceConstraints: Preserve tentative progress and avoid a grand discovery about courage.

sourceObjectiveEvidence.quote: Read this personal essay for distracting clarity problems. Keep any changes minimal, and preserve the calendar heading "one lane at a time." exactly.
At my first swimming lesson, the instructor asked what I wanted to learn.
